reason: The earlier conclusion that all 114 members are the same person still holds, and no member is pruned. The only substantive change is to three member signatures (jinshu:020:p092, jinshu:086:p072 and jiutangshu:029:p125). Their name keys for 武帝, 世祖, 'Emperor Shizu' and 'Shizu' change kind from personal to posthumous-name or temple-name, and from blocking to nonblocking. I approved those five kind corrections against the primary Chinese. No name string, preferred name (Sima Yan / 司馬炎), role, family link, mention count or date hint is added or removed. The identity of these three members never rested on treating 世祖 or 武帝 as a personal name. It rests on the actual Chinese contexts. In Jinshu 020, Emperor Wu's empress Yang Dao raised 懷帝 and is not paired in the 世祖 temple. In Jinshu 086, the 世祖 whose grandson is addressed is a Jin ancestor of the 晉人. In Jiutangshu 029, 懷帝 is said to succeed 世祖 rather than 惠帝. Jinshu 003 ties these labels to one emperor: it names the annals subject as 武皇帝諱炎 and records 廟號世祖. So 世祖 (temple name) and 武帝 (posthumous name) both point to the Western Jin founder 炎, and the existing basis already chains them for the whole group (世祖武皇帝, 武帝受禪, the 惠帝/愍懷 family links). Reclassifying these labels as imperial names supports the merge; it does not weaken it. The other 111 signatures change only in renumbered claim-pointer provenance. I treat their hashes only as binding unchanged dependencies, not as new identity evidence, and the prior source-reviewed basis for them stands as before. The 79 candidate comparisons removed under the existing nonblocking temple/posthumous rules are all pairs of the merged Jin Wu cluster against other people. They remove no member and add no pair. The native validator reports that all prior canonical memberships are unchanged and that the strong-name evidence for all 114 members still passes, which agrees with this reading.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
帝崩于含章殿，時年五十五，葬峻陽陵，廟號世祖。
武帝楊悼皇后既母養懷帝
晉惠帝無後，懷帝承統，懷帝自繼于世祖，而不繼于惠帝。
